changed.title: Every circuit selecting a satisfying cyclic word needs NOT gates to distinguish incomparable block words
changed.statement:
∀ (n w k : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n), 0 < k → k ≤ n → k ≤ w + 1 →
  let stride := 2 ^ (w + 1)
  let I := n * stride
  ∀ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (outBit : Fin n → Fin (I + C.size)),
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C →
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack I C →
    (∀ table : Fin n → (Fin (w + 1) → Bool) → Bool,
      let inputs := List.ofFn (fun addr : Fin I =>
        table ⟨(addr.val / stride) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩ (fun b => addr.val.testBit b.val))
      let valid := fun (word : Fin n → Bool) => ∀ i : Fin n,
        table i (fun j => word ⟨(i.val + j.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩) = true
      (∃ word, valid word) →
        valid (fun pos => (C.wires inputs).getD (outBit pos).val false)) →
    1 + (n / k) * (Nat.choose k (k / 2) - 1) ≤ 2 ^ PEqualNP.NotBracket.notCount C
changed.unlocks: prices negations needed by any circuit returning a valid solution on satisfiable tables
changed.context: Use floor(n/k) disjoint blocks. A table at each block start admits a subset of the middle-weight k-bit words, ignoring extra bits. Other rows accept all. Shrink one subset by deleting the current witness block until one word remains, then move on. All tables stay satisfiable. Each change exchanges incomparable block words, so reversing the chain gives an output drop at every step. If previous wires have D dropping steps, AND/OR add none. A NOT adds at most one per increasing interval, giving at most 2D+1. Start at zero drops.
